hotSpots.description: HS1/HS2: pilots are to maintain a good lookout at all times and are responsible for wing tip clearance. HS3: pilots of Code F aircraft must take care - Link 28 east of Taxiway Alpha is NOT Code F compliant. HS4: pilots are to ensure they have clearance to enter the runway before crossing the holding point. HS5: mis-route hotspot - after vacating the runway, pilots to be aware of the potential to mis-route. (AD 2-EGLL-2-1) Caution on the diagram: BE ALERT TO RUNWAY CROSSING CLEARANCES. READBACK OF ALL RUNWAY HOLDING INSTRUCTIONS IS REQUIRED.

runwayConfigurations.name: Westerly: land 27R (northern), depart 27L (southern)
runwayConfigurations.notes: Westerly segregated mode of operations. AD 2.20 para 6 (Preferential Runway System): "In weather conditions when the tail wind component is no greater than 5 KT on the main Runway 27R and 27L, these runways will normally be used in preference to Runways 09R and 09L, provided the runway(s) surface is dry." Runway alternation (operator, not the AIP): one runway for landings and the other for take-offs, swapped at 15:00 local; the pair swaps every week. Programme 2026: landings on 27R 06:00-15:00 and on 27L from 15:00 until the last departure in the weeks commencing 12 Jan, 26 Jan, ... (odd weeks counted from 5 Jan 2026), the reverse in the other weeks (see alternation_programme_2026). 06:00-07:00 both runways may land (not modelled). AD 2.20 para 4 warns of building-induced turbulence on 27R in strong southerly/south-westerly winds; the operator moves landings to the southern runway in that case. Simulator note: configurations are chosen by headwind (src/weather/runwayConfigurations.ts); the time-of-day alternation between W-ALT-27R and W-ALT-27L is not selected automatically (list order: 27R first, the programme state in the week of 2026-10-19 until 15:00).

provenance.source: UK AIP AIRAC 10/2026 AD 2.20 para 6 and para 4; AD 2.22

runwayConfigurations.name: Westerly: land 27L (southern), depart 27R (northern)
runwayConfigurations.notes: The other half of the westerly alternation (see W-ALT-27R): landings on 27L 06:00-15:00 in the weeks commencing 5 Jan, 19 Jan, ... (even weeks counted from 5 Jan 2026) and on 27R in the afternoon. Tactically Enhanced Arrivals Mode (TEAM, operator page): after 07:00 on westerly operations, up to six arrivals an hour may land on the departure runway when delays of 20 minutes or more are expected (not modelled). Simulator note: configurations are chosen by headwind (src/weather/runwayConfigurations.ts); the time-of-day alternation between W-ALT-27R and W-ALT-27L is not selected automatically (list order: 27R first, the programme state in the week of 2026-10-19 until 15:00).

provenance.source: Heathrow Airport Limited, "Runway alternation" page and Runway Alternation Programme 2026 (operator publication, not the AIP)

runwayConfigurations.name: Easterly: land 09L (northern), depart 09R (southern)
runwayConfigurations.notes: Easterly operations (used when the 5 kt tailwind limit on 27 is exceeded). Operator page: "On easterly operations, we do not alternate the runways at 15:00 because of the Cranford Agreement which prevented us from using the northern runway for departures during the day. Although the Cranford Agreement has now ended, we need to undertake works to the airport's infrastructure before runway alternation on easterly operations will be possible." and "aircraft cannot take off towards the east from the northern runway" (status of the Cranford Agreement: ended, not yet exploited, as published by the operator on the retrieval date). The AIP publishes no Cranford text; it gives ILS and noise rules for both ends. AD 2.20 para 6: pilots asking for the runway into wind when 27 is in use "should understand that their arrival or departure may be delayed". Simulator note: configurations are chosen by headwind (src/weather/runwayConfigurations.ts); the time-of-day alternation between W-ALT-27R and W-ALT-27L is not selected automatically (list order: 27R first, the programme state in the week of 2026-10-19 until 15:00).

remarks: Types of traffic permitted: IFR/VFR/SVFR (AD 2.2 item 8).
Telephone calls to NATS Ltd operational areas may be recorded.
Stand 357 has block paving; all other aprons concrete.
Nose-in parking throughout; A-VDGS on most stands; MARS and Multi Choice Apron stands exist (stand number with L/R for MARS sub-centrelines).

Hot spots: HS1/HS2 maintain a good lookout, wing tip clearance is the pilot's responsibility; HS3 Link 28 east of Taxiway Alpha is not Code F compliant; HS4 ensure clearance to enter the runway before crossing the holding point; HS5 mis-route hot spot after vacating runway.
Green taxiway centre-line lights with selective switching, red stop bars controlled from the Tower, runway guard lights H24.
Pilots report type, stand number, QNH and the ATIS identification letter on first contact with Heathrow Delivery.
Taxiway Yankee between HANLI and Taxiway Alpha is restricted to Code C; Link 56 to Code D.
Helicopter operations: PPR; crossing procedures between Sipson/Bedfont/Feltham; helicopter aiming point east of Link 43.
